summary.text: Consolidated stage1/ATT/INV success criteria: use eight invented records; only K2/K5/K7 become checked, all others remain unchecked; source scores stay read-only; no incorrect-key write counts as acceptable even if repaired. Finish sequential actions within ten simulated minutes with the latest snapshot loaded.

Candidate C, shared by stage1, ATT and INV, is a hypothesis: keep S0 loaded; inspect/select and commit K2 during 0-2, K5 during 2-4, K7 during 4-6; refresh during 6-7. Predicted writes use rows 2/5/7, then S2 preserves statuses by key. Verified success would refute per-commit refresh necessity within this model; it has not been replayed.

Stage1 alternatives remain hypotheses: A repeats refresh, inspect explicit key, commit during 0-3/3-6/6-9, with refresh completions 1/4/7. B uses synthetic immutable-key binding and repeats inspect, refresh, commit, with refresh completions 2/5/8. Both predict correct writes and final S2 at nine minutes. Concerns require identity stability across reordering; production key binding is unestablished.

Stage1 verification and ATT/INV concerns consolidate into independent replays from all-unchecked S0: log times, refreshes, loaded snapshots, displayed order, selected rows, intended keys and every actual key/value. Compare all candidates against exact final statuses, unchanged source scores, zero wrong-key writes, final freshness and elapsed time. These measurements would test predictions; no replay outcome is asserted.
